nodes.title: Verbose RTFM
widgets_values:
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

If you get a blurry grid glitch, your embedding is OOD (out of distribution for latent / feature space of diffusion transformer).

-> reduce factor for subtraction, or add a vector in addition.
For example: Extreme subtraction of 'cars' from 'new york city streets' leads to OOD before cars are fully gone -> add "new york, empty streets"
-> This example is included as a workflow with my node!
-> Try: Set clip_addvec_alpha to 0 -> Result: Not-yet-a-glitch, but nearing the OOD zone; it's evident by blurriness and loss of details.
-> Try: Also increase minusvec_alpha, you'll see the 'grid-glitch' of OOD

----------------------------------------------------------------------------

If you have many vectors (5 prompts or more) to subtract with clip_l_minusvec, e.g. red|pink|rose|crimson|orange, 
it **would** very likely lead to a 'glitch'. Alas:

-> I am getting the principal components (PCA) that best describe this accumulation of negatives, say (simplified analogy) a red direction, a muted color direction, and a yellow direction as the most important directions for the above simplified example -> only subtract these -> reduce glitch risk.

-> PRO TIP!
If you get a glitch with e.g. just 3 clip_l_minusvec, you can just repeat the same ones and 'auto-trigger' PCA with 5 or more, e.g.: 
red|pink|rose|red|pink|rose. 

With PCA, it's basically a 'softer', less radical subtraction, as we "group" the things that are very very similar, instead of radically subtracting them all.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------

simple_neg: If True, your vectors will be subtracted in order, e.g. car|vehicle -> subtract car. Then subtract vehicle. More extreme result, very high glitch risk, but may be useful for certain cases.

If False, projects and subtracts subspace (orthogonal projection onto the null space); basically does everything 'nicely and at the same time', without piling up negatives upon negatives.

Kind of like when you train a model: You backpropagate and update *all* weights of a model together to not end up in some weird only-local minimum specific for a batch that ruins everything by 'piling up extremes'.

nodes.title: Quick Reference
widgets_values:
clip_l: --------------->
        CLIP-L normal prompt

        
  
     

        t5xxl:----------------->
        T5 normal prompt

        



        clip_l_minusvec: ------>
        vector(s) to subtract
        use | as separator

       

       clip_l_addvec: --------->
       vector(s) to add
       use | as separator



       t5xxl_minusvec: -------->
       not a good idea.
       wrecks embedding.
       use "semantic negative"
       as below:


      t5xxl_addvec: ----------->
      instead of minusvec,
      use a semantic 
      negative and add:
      "cars" -> "without cars"



ALL: If text empty or alpha = 0
---> DISABLED.
---------------------------------
- Use "minusvec" and "addvec" to do a proper 'difference vector':

Example:

clip_l and t5xxl both prompts:
"a photo of a king"

clip_l_minusvec = "man"
clip_l_addvec   = "woman"

both clip_****_alpha = 1.1

-> king - man + woman = queen
---------------------------------

simple_neg: subtract negatives in-order. If False: orthogonal projection onto the null space

nuke_*** = set input to 0, disable this text encoder.

randn_*** = random (noise) guidance instead of normal embedding.
